title: Mid-Term Functional Neurological Outcome After Successful Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Following Cardiac Arrest – A Retrospective Study
summary:
This exploratory, single-center retrospective study aims to establish and analyze a registry of patients treated between January 2015 and April 2024 in the interdisciplinary medical intensive care units (IMIT) at the University Medical Center Freiburg following successful cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) after cardiac arrest.
The primary focus is on patients who, after stabilization and completion of acute care, were transferred to specialized inpatient neurological rehabilitation.
The primary endpoint is the neurological outcome (CPC score) at the time of discharge from neurological rehabilitation.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who, between January 1, 2015 and April 30, 2024, were transferred to inpatient neurological rehabilitation after successful resuscitation following cardiac arrest and subsequent treatment in the intensive care unit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who were treated during the data collection period on the wards MIT 1, MIT 2 (formerly Heilmeyer I and Heilmeyer II), and de la Camp (IMIT) following intra- or extrahospital cardiac arrest are to be included in the research project described here.
The primary analysis includes those patients from the overall group who were transferred to inpatient neurological rehabilitation treatment after successful acute care.
Exclusion criteria:
none
